sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Spalding County?
sections.html:
Spalding County splits the work across several offices. The Tax Commissioner bills, collects and disburses the tax. The Board of Tax Assessors sets values, approves exemptions and receives appeals. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears appeals the assessors cannot settle, and the county commissioners and the school board set the millage rates.

The Tax Commissioner's office is at 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, a few blocks from the courthouse, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at (770) 467-4360, with a mailing address of PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224. The Tax Assessor's phone line is (770) 467-4240. County government offices are at 119 E. Solomon Street.

sections.h2: When are Spalding County property taxes due, and what happens when they are late?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property taxes are normally due November 15. The Tax Commissioner says no late fees are charged until 60 days after the bills are mailed. After the due date, interest accrues monthly at the legal rate, and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days until it reaches 20%.

Homesteaded property with a tax liability under $500 does not receive the penalty. Mobile and modular homes follow a different calendar: tax is due April 1, and the owner must file a return and pay in full to obtain a location permit. If taxes stay unpaid, the Tax Commissioner can levy on the property, and the office describes that as a last resort.

sections.h2: What are the key Spalding County tax rules at a glance?
sections.html:
Spalding County property tax rules, from the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's website
TopicRule as the county prints it
Assessed value40% of fair market value
Tax return windowJanuary 1 to April 1 each year
Real estate bill dueNovember 15
Appeal period45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed
Homestead applicationMust be received before April 1 to count for that year
Mobile home taxDue April 1
Tax sale timingFirst Tuesday of the month, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

One mill equals $1.00 for each $1,000 of assessed value, and the bill is figured by subtracting exemptions from the 40% assessed value and then applying the millage rate.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Spalding County assessment?
sections.html:
File within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. The county says appeals can rest on taxability, value or uniformity of value compared with similar properties, and not on a complaint about the size of the tax bill.

The appeal goes first to the Board of Tax Assessors. If you stay dissatisfied, it moves to the county Board of Equalization, or you can choose arbitration, and a further appeal goes to Superior Court. For 2026, the county's Tax Commissioner site said the homestead window matched the 45 day appeal window, running June 5 through July 23, 2026, so that window has closed for this year. Income based exemptions must be applied for in person with proof of 2025 income.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Spalding County offer?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner lists state and local exemptions combined. The main ones:

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 each from the state, county and school portions, with no income test.
  • Standard elderly, age 65 and over before January 1, net income at or below $15,000, with larger county and school deductions.
  • School exemption, age 62 and over or totally disabled, household gross income at or below $12,500.
  • Ages 65 to 69, $10,000 off the school portion regardless of income; ages 70 to 74, $20,000; ages 75 and older, $30,000.
  • A floating exemption on the school portion for owners 65 and older, which freezes the value used for school tax.

Once granted, an exemption renews each year until the owner moves or qualifies for a different type. A buyer must apply for the new address. The county also offers a deferral for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, which can run until ownership changes or the deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a deferral lien exists on a house before you sell it.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Spalding County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 70,775 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.2% from the 2020 base, and counts 29,850 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home value is $228,700, the owner-occupied rate is 62.7% and median gross rent is $1,113. Median household income is $62,071, and 20.6% of residents are 65 or older, which makes the senior exemptions above relevant to many sellers.

The county covers 195.97 square miles of land at 343.5 people per square mile, and Griffin is where the courthouse, tax office and clerk sit. The county's own news page notes a comprehensive plan update that looks toward 2050 and the county commissioners' adoption of a full rollback rate for 2025, which can come up in buyer conversations.

sections.h2: How are delinquent taxes and tax sales handled in Spalding County?
sections.html:
Georgia law, as the Tax Commissioner's FAQ puts it, places tax sales on the first Tuesday of the month between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Sales are held at 411 E. Solomon Street, bidder registration runs from 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. on sale day, and bidders must be 18 or older with photo ID. Bidding usually opens between 10:00 and 10:30 a.m.

Notices run in the Griffin Daily News on Tuesdays starting four weeks before a sale, and the office posts the sale list on its site. Excess funds requests for tax sale proceeds need original documents, and the office accepts no email. If a house you own faces a sale, contact the Tax Commissioner before the advertising starts.

sections.h2: Where do I record the deed or get a copy in Spalding County?
sections.html:
The Clerk of Superior Court keeps deeds. The clerk's office is at 132 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., at 770-467-4309, with a deputy clerk assigned to real estate. The Tax Commissioner's FAQ sends owners there for a copy of a warranty deed.

Spalding County's Community Development department at 119 E. Solomon Street covers planning, zoning and permits for unincorporated Spalding County. Its Planning Commission meets the last Tuesday of the month at 6:00 p.m., and its Board of Appeals meets the second Thursday of the month at 6:00 p.m. Call the department before you start repair work if the house sits outside the city of Griffin. Its contact list also names a business and alcohol license technician and a permit technician, so ask for the right desk when you call.

faqs.q: When are Spalding County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 for real estate and business personal property. The Tax Commissioner says no late fees are charged until 60 days after the bills are mailed. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal a Spalding County assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. The appeal is filed with the Board of Tax Assessors and can move to the Board of Equalization, arbitration and then Superior Court.

faqs.q: What is the Spalding County late penalty?
faqs.a: Interest runs monthly at the legal rate after the due date, plus a 5% penalty every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 is excused from the penalty.

faqs.q: Where is the Spalding County Tax Commissioner's office?
faqs.a: 411 E. Solomon Street in Griffin, GA 30223, reachable at (770) 467-4360, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The mailing address is PO Box 509, Griffin, GA 30224.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spalding County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the Tax Commissioner can levy on unpaid property and sell it at a tax sale. Ask the office for the total owed, including interest and penalties, so the balance is paid from your closing proceeds.
